_comment: The frontmatter contract, in the form a script can read.
It is deliberately SEPARATE from SKILL-FRONTMATTER.md, and the two are gated against each
other by lint_skills.py --self-test: every governance field named in the prose table must
appear in 'fields' here, and vice versa. A schema documented in one place and enforced in
another is two schemas that agree until the day somebody edits one of them.
EVERY GOVERNANCE FIELD LIVES UNDER 'metadata'. That is not tidiness -- it is what makes the
same file portable. A skill distributed outside the CLI is validated against a fixed field
list, and an unrecognised TOP-LEVEL key is rejected outright rather than ignored. 'metadata'
is the sanctioned free-form map, so a governance block nested there travels; the same fields
hoisted to the top level do not. See SKILL-FRONTMATTER.md for the dated source.
PROFILES exist because one tree is usually not one contract. A curated catalogue wants an
owner and a review date; a generated bundle wants an invocation name and nothing else.
Requiring the catalogue's block everywhere fails every file in the second tree and invents
governance that tree does not use -- which is how a gate stops being read.
_description_max_chars_note: A CONVENTION, not a platform limit, and labelled as one on purpose. The platform's own cap
is larger and is a truncation rather than a rejection -- see SKILL-FRONTMATTER.md, which
carries the figure with the date it was checked. Set this to whatever your catalogue can
defend; the check reports the number back so a reader can see which one they are held to.
_placeholder_values_note: A required field filled with 'TBD' is not a filled field. Without this list the gate passes
on a template nobody completed, which is worse than no gate: it certifies the placeholder.

fields.owner: The person answerable for the skill. A name, not a team, so the question 'who decides?' has one answer.
fields.backup_owner: Who answers when the owner cannot. Empty is honest; absent is not.
fields.approved_by: Who accepted this into the catalogue. CATALOGUE GOVERNANCE ONLY -- it is not a security or legal approval, and it confers nothing on anything the skill reviews.
fields.approval_date: When that acceptance happened. ISO date.
fields.review_date: When it must be looked at again. ISO date. A skill past its review date is a claim nobody has re-checked.
fields.sunset_date: When it stops being current. Empty while live. Sunset by BANNER, never by deletion -- the file is a deliberate record of what was once advised.
fields.risk_tier: How much it can do, on a scale you define. Honest tiering is the whole value; a catalogue where everything is tier 1 has measured nothing.
fields.risk_factors: The SPECIFIC residual risk, the mechanism that bounds it, and the test that asserts the mechanism. All three, or it is a ritual.
fields.pii_handling: What personal data it touches, and what it does with it. 'None' is a valid answer and must still be stated.
fields.changelog_url: Where its history can be read. A pointer at nothing is worse than no pointer.
fields.eval_pass_rate: Measured triggering accuracy, written back by eval_skills.py. Never hand-edited.
fields.eval_last_run: When that measurement was taken. A rate with no date is a claim about now.

profiles.name: catalogue
note: 'name' is NOT in required_top, and that is a deliberate departure from the rule this was
extracted from. The CLI does not require it and does not derive the command from it in a
personal or project skill -- the directory name does that, and 'name' is a display label.
So requiring it enforces a house style, which is fine, but calling it a platform rule is
not. It is checked WHEN PRESENT (name_matches_directory) and not demanded when absent.
Add it to required_top if your catalogue wants it; the point is that the choice is yours
and is visible here rather than hardcoded in a script.

profiles.name: bundle
note: A generated bundle: files produced from a source tree by a generator. Two things change.
'name' IS required here, because in a PLUGIN SKILL -- the documentation's term for what
this profile calls a bundle -- it sets the last segment of the command rather than a
display label, so a mismatch means the command a user types and the skill that answers
have drifted apart. And the governance block is deliberately NOT required: no generated
file carries one, so demanding it would fail every file and invent a contract nobody keeps.
'slash_command' is NOT required, and that is the correction this profile most needed. It
is not one of the six frontmatter fields accepted outside the CLI, so a file carrying it
fails packaging or upload with a HARD ERROR rather than having the key ignored -- exactly
the trap the comment at the top of this file warns about. Requiring it made the schema
mandate the one thing the prose beside it says never to do. It is also repo-local
vocabulary that leaked in when this schema was generalised out of a single plugin bundle.
So it is a DELIBERATE LOCAL EXTENSION: checked when present, never demanded. A tree that
chooses to carry it gets slash_command_matches_directory enforced against the directory; a
tree that does not carry it passes. That is the treatment 'name' already gets in the
catalogue profile, for the same reason. The trade-off a local extension makes -- a local
convenience bought with portability outside the CLI -- is now visible here rather than
latent in a required_top nobody read.
Why lint a generated tree at all: a generator proves its output matches its input, and a
parity check that strips frontmatter before diffing proves nothing about the frontmatter.
A malformed-but-faithfully-generated file passes both. This is the check that does not.
